irb-ganga-capital-recycling.summary: A ₹1,746 crore lowest-grant award led to MBEL’s ₹6,538 crore financing plan. IRB retained EPC and O&M roles while GIC affiliate Anahera held 49%. In December 2024, IRB Infrastructure Trust acquired 80.4% of equity and debentures for ₹1,714.92 crore combined consideration. This documents capital recycling; it does not establish a political favour.

adani-ganga-financing.summary: Groups II–IV are held by Budaun Hardoi, Hardoi Unnao and Unnao Prayagraj Road companies. The 29 September 2022 exchange filing disaggregates ₹10,238 crore senior debt, ₹6,826 crore company equity and ₹5,996 crore VGF. UPEIDA independently confirms group-specific lowest-grant selection; the lender identity comes from the borrower filing.

lnt-c4-jica-finance.summary: The official C4 award contains ₹21,239.9562767 crore, JPY 878.236238 million and USD 495.520952 million. NHSRCL is the buyer and public SPV. JICA’s cumulative JPY 1,050 billion commitment by 21 December 2023 is to the Government of India for the whole MAHSR project. This separates the package contract, public ownership, executing agency and sovereign finance.
lnt-c4-jica-finance.period: 2 December 2019 ownership statement; 26 November 2020 C4 agreement; 21 December 2023 latest loan tranche retained
lnt-c4-jica-finance.falsifier: Join each C4 payment certificate and FX clause to JICA disbursement applications and NHSRCL accounts. Without those records, the whole project loan cannot be attributed to L&T.
alternativeExplanations: ODA project loans commonly fund multiple contracts through a sovereign borrower and executing SPV.
The rounded ₹24,985 crore press headline depends on currency conversion; this case uses the three contract components.
limitations: No cross-currency sum and no whole-project loan allocation to C4.
The original NHSRCL server returned HTTP 503; exact indexed official register text is retained.
No overall project-completion claim is made. Scheduled construction duration does not establish completion.

rec-apgenco-loan.summary: CAG paragraph 3.2.3 records that APGENCO obtained a ₹3,965.11 crore term loan at 11% to fund the debt portion of PHEP’s ₹4,956.39 crore cost. The loan is not an additional contractor payment.

amounts.stage: project term loan obtained; drawdown schedule not retained

apgenco-meil-contract.label: PHEP electromechanical contract
apgenco-meil-contract.summary: CAG paragraph 3.2.3 identifies a March 2021 agreement at ₹2,810.88 crore; footnote 148 names MEIL. This component differs from the 2019 combined headworks and powerhouse bid.
apgenco-meil-contract.dateBasis: March 2021 only; exact signing day not retained.

amounts.stage: electromechanical contract price; not paid amount

apgenco-meil-advance.label: ₹30.86 crore material advances paid
apgenco-meil-advance.summary: CAG paragraph 3.2.2.1 records ₹30.86 crore paid during December 2021–October 2022 for steel after the November 2021 amendment. Government disputes the advance characterisation; CAG estimates ₹1.10 crore foregone interest.
apgenco-meil-advance.falsifier: Board-approved price breakups, original and amended clauses, steel receipt and incorporation records, and an accepted PAC settlement could resolve the payment characterisation.
alternativeExplanations: Government says a Board-approved split-price schedule permitted payment when steel reached the site.

amounts.stage: material advance payments recorded by audit

cag-material-finding.label: Audit: interest-free material advance favoured contractor
cag-material-finding.summary: CAG concludes payment should have followed finished work and calculates ₹1.10 crore foregone interest for December 2021–November 2022. This is an attributed audit finding, not a criminal verdict.

amounts.stage: auditor-estimated foregone interest; not principal loss

limitations: The ₹1.10 crore interest estimate cannot be added to ₹30.86 crore as stolen funds.

cag-equipment-finding.label: Audit: ₹41.26 crore early equipment procurement
cag-equipment-finding.summary: CAG paragraph 3.2.3 records ₹41.26 crore of equipment procured during June 2022–June 2023 and lying idle 28–428 days beyond the allowed six months. It estimates ₹1.90 crore additional interest through February 2024. Government cites design changes and early BHEL equipment supply.
limitations: No separate BHEL contract or payment edge is drawn: the government’s mention does not establish specific subcontract amounts.
Do not sum equipment procurement with material advances; potential invoice overlap remains unresolved.

amounts.stage: equipment procurement value described by audit; not all project spending
audit estimate of additional financing interest

meil-polavaram-response.summary: Government replies in August and November 2024 say steel payments followed Board-approved split prices and receipt at site; clauses were inserted at the contractor’s request to mobilise funds. CAG rejects this as an interest-free advance for unfinished work. At the November 2024 exit conference, government accepted the separate early-equipment observation while explaining design changes and early BHEL supply; CAG rejected that justification because procurement should follow installation need. Parliament on 6 August 2026 reaffirmed that Andhra Pradesh bears the powerhouse cost, while central Phase I grants cover irrigation, land acquisition and rehabilitation.
meil-polavaram-response.period: Government replies August and November 2024; report published 6 March 2026; parliamentary answer 6 August 2026
meil-polavaram-response.response: No later accepted audit settlement, recovery order or criminal adjudication of these specific findings was retrieved. The 2026 parliamentary answer does not settle them.
alternativeExplanations: Supply-stage payments can legitimately finance work when authorised; the dispute here concerns post-award amendment and finished-work rules.
Design changes can explain misaligned delivery but do not by themselves disprove financing costs.
meil-polavaram-response.falsifier: Retrieve Board minutes, Amendment No. 2, original schedule, steel and equipment invoices, installation dates, loan interest ledger and post-audit PAC action-taken reports.

meil-polavaram-working-capital.summary: CAG links MEIL’s ₹2,810.88 crore equipment contract to APGENCO’s REC-financed powerhouse. It records ₹30.86 crore steel advances after a contract amendment and estimates ₹1.10 crore foregone interest. Separately, ₹41.26 crore premature equipment procurement generated an estimated ₹1.90 crore financing interest. Government contests the advance characterisation; it accepted the early-equipment observation while explaining design changes.
meil-polavaram-working-capital.period: March 2021 equipment agreement; November 2021 amendment; advances December 2021–October 2022; equipment June 2022–June 2023; interest through February 2024; government replies 2024; publication 2026
meil-polavaram-working-capital.response: The linked response preserves the government’s authorised-stage-payment defence and CAG’s rejoinder. The latest parliamentary answer keeps powerhouse funding separate from central irrigation grants; it does not resolve the audit dispute.
alternativeExplanations: Board-approved material payments could have a commercial cash-flow justification; the audit question is compliance with post-award terms and interest treatment.
Delay and design revision can explain idle components without establishing diversion.
meil-polavaram-working-capital.falsifier: Reconstruct each invoice’s supply, inspection, installation, payment and loan-interest dates and check the authority for Amendment No. 2. A later accepted reconciliation or adjudication could narrow or reverse the finding.
limitations: These are audit findings, not criminal adjudication. No political quid pro quo is inferred and no electoral-bond payment is joined to the award.
Loan, contract, advance, equipment and interest amounts are separate stages with potential overlap; do not sum them.
Report 4 of 2025 was published on 6 March 2026; most financial events and government responses are much older.
Official indexed text was retained after the original host returned HTTP 503; exact paragraph locators and failure receipts are preserved.

amounts.stage: APGENCO project term loan obtained from REC
audit-estimated foregone interest on material advances
separate early equipment procurement value described by audit
audit-estimated additional interest on early equipment

zojila-exact-id-lead.summary: Original CPPP notice 2020_NHIDC_564017_1 and reference NHIDCL/JnK-Ladakh/ Zojila/NH-01/2020 are accessible. NHIDCL’s project register separately names MEIL and award date 25 August 2020. The exact ID/reference query against the supplied snapshot returned zero rows. This is a coverage gap, not proof of no award.
zojila-exact-id-lead.period: Notice June 2020; authority award date 25 August 2020; corpus snapshot 26 June 2026
zojila-exact-id-lead.response: No allegation is advanced. Varying news bid figures and the current project cost need original award and contract reconciliation.
alternativeExplanations: The database capture can omit a valid award or format its reference differently.
A revised project cost may include scope, land or other items absent from an EPC bid.
zojila-exact-id-lead.falsifier: Obtain the signed letter of award and EPC agreement for the exact notice, verify legal identity and price or corrigenda, then join milestone certificates and paid bills.
limitations: The ₹4,429.83 crore notice estimate and current project cost are not categorised as payments.
UT geography is not assigned from ambiguous legacy JK state codes.
